also: take your shoes off before going in
leave your shoes at the door

phrases.latin: Puer, calceīs, pilleō, paenulā dētractīs, in lectum suum positus est
phrases.english: The boy, his shoes, cap, and coat taken off, was put into his own bed
phrases.source: Libellus VI, Reditus: per Alpēs domum

phrases.latin: Calceōs in līmine exue; nōn licet calceātum intrāre.
phrases.english: Take your shoes off at the door; you may not go in with your shoes on.

phrases.latin: solve calceāmentum dē pedibus tuīs: locus enim, in quō stās, terra sāncta est
phrases.english: take your shoes off your feet, for the place where you are standing is holy ground

sources: Lewis & Short: exuo · Lewis & Short: detraho
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 118, 400.
Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word.
